scope: Plain-English contractor readiness for Australian, Queensland and Commonwealth procurement. Every live approach to market can add, remove or change requirements.
public_boundary: This data is general information, not legal, tax, financial, insurance, engineering or procurement advice. Check the live tender pack and obtain professional advice before forming an entity, signing a collaboration agreement or accepting a contract.

vehicle_options.title: Sole trader
vehicle_options.best_fit: Testing small, lower-risk services where one person genuinely controls and delivers the work.
vehicle_options.watch: You carry the business debts and liabilities personally. A larger or higher-risk contract may justify a different structure.

vehicle_options.title: Company
vehicle_options.best_fit: A separate legal entity for an ongoing delivery business, staff, assets, partners and larger contractual risk.
vehicle_options.watch: Directors have legal duties. The company needs an ACN, its own ABN and TFN, annual review and proper records.

vehicle_options.title: Queensland incorporated association
vehicle_options.best_fit: A not-for-profit community group with at least 7 members, a committee, rules and a Queensland address.
vehicle_options.watch: It is a legal entity and can contract, but its not-for-profit purpose, rules, reporting and committee authority still control what it may do.

vehicle_options.title: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander corporation
vehicle_options.best_fit: A First Nations-controlled corporation formed under the CATSI Act with an appropriate membership and governance base.
vehicle_options.watch: This is a real governance choice, not a procurement shortcut. ORIC registration and Indigenous Procurement Policy eligibility have their own rules.

vehicle_options.title: Partner, consortium or subcontract route
vehicle_options.best_fit: A group or young business contributes a clear delivery lane while a capable existing entity leads the contract.
vehicle_options.watch: Use a written agreement. The prime remains answerable to government and usually remains responsible for subcontracted work.

universal_baseline.title: Legal identity and signing authority
universal_baseline.plain_rule: Name the exact legal entity that will tender and the person authorised to bind it.
universal_baseline.evidence: Legal name, ABN, ACN or incorporation number, registered address, governing-rule check and written delegation or board resolution where needed.

universal_baseline.title: Business and tax registrations
universal_baseline.plain_rule: Hold the registrations that apply to the chosen structure and expected turnover.
universal_baseline.evidence: ABN, TFN, business name if needed, GST status, PAYG withholding status and director ID for company directors.

universal_baseline.title: Licences, permits and professional registrations
universal_baseline.plain_rule: The people and entities doing regulated work must hold the right current authority for that work and location.
universal_baseline.evidence: Licence register extracts, certificates, qualifications, RPEQ or other professional registration and an expiry register.

universal_baseline.title: Insurance matched to the contract
universal_baseline.plain_rule: Do not guess the cover. Check the tender's types, limits, exclusions, territory, run-off period and subcontractor conditions.
universal_baseline.evidence: Current certificates of currency and broker confirmation for public liability, professional indemnity, workers compensation, motor, cyber or contract works where required.

universal_baseline.title: Workforce law, safety and super
universal_baseline.plain_rule: Classify workers honestly, pay lawful entitlements, manage WHS and hold workers compensation cover where required.
universal_baseline.evidence: Employment or contractor records, awards check, payroll and super records, WHS system, incident process and WorkCover policy.

universal_baseline.title: Financial capacity and cashflow
universal_baseline.plain_rule: Show that the entity can fund wages, materials, travel, insurance, reporting and delays until payment arrives.
universal_baseline.evidence: Costed price, cashflow forecast, accounts, tax status, credit or finance plan and financial-capacity evidence requested by the buyer.

universal_baseline.title: Capability and delivery proof
universal_baseline.plain_rule: Evidence must support the exact scope being promised.
universal_baseline.evidence: Comparable projects, outcomes, photos with permission, referees, key-person CVs, methods, equipment, quality controls and honest limits.

universal_baseline.title: Privacy, confidentiality and cyber safety
universal_baseline.plain_rule: Keep tender material, personal information, buyer data, credentials and commercial-in-confidence records in the correct private system.
universal_baseline.evidence: Access controls, data map, backup and retention rules, incident process, approved AI-use boundary and contract-specific security controls.

universal_baseline.title: Conflicts, probity and truthful declarations
universal_baseline.plain_rule: Declare actual, potential and perceived conflicts. Never collude, offer inducements or invent compliance.
universal_baseline.evidence: Conflict register, declarations, gifts policy, bid-team confidentiality rules and a record of assumptions and clarifications.

universal_baseline.title: Contract and risk review
universal_baseline.plain_rule: Read the proposed contract before pricing and before saying yes.
universal_baseline.evidence: Reviewed departures, indemnity and liability position, intellectual property, insurance, payment, security, variation, termination, dispute and recordkeeping obligations.

queensland.title: Create the Queensland supplier profile
queensland.applies_when: General market visibility and supplier registration.
queensland.action: Create and maintain a free Supplier Portal profile with accurate categories and contact details; separately use QTenders and the forward pipeline.

queensland.title: Self-assess against the Supplier Code
queensland.applies_when: All Queensland Government procurement activities, regardless of value.
queensland.action: Check legal compliance, ethics, workplace practices, human rights, environment, conflicts, records and supply-chain behaviour before giving the tender warranty.

queensland.title: Prepare for procurement assurance
queensland.applies_when: Working under a Queensland Government contract from 1 January 2026.
queensland.action: Retain evidence of Code compliance. Principal contractors must flow Code obligations and measurable purposeful-procurement commitments into subcontracts.

queensland.title: Answer only the relevant public-purpose outcomes
queensland.applies_when: The quote or tender includes local, economic, environmental, social or governance outcomes.
queensland.action: Use specific, costed and measurable commitments. Do not promise every policy objective. Significant procurement uses a weighted purposeful-procurement criterion unless a reason is documented.

queensland.title: Check building prequalification
queensland.applies_when: Direct Queensland Government building contracts over $1 million, or covered building consultancy commissions.
queensland.action: Check PQC eligibility, licences, experience, ethical-supplier evidence and financial capacity before treating the tender as leadable.

queensland.title: Use the minor works and maintenance route
queensland.applies_when: QBuild minor works, service maintenance or work below the PQC major-project threshold.
queensland.action: Register with QBuild and meet the category, licence, insurance and contract requirements for the work offered.

queensland.title: Check civil and transport schemes
queensland.applies_when: Road, bridge, asphalt or specialist transport infrastructure work.
queensland.action: Check the TMR Infrastructure Project Delivery System and National Prequalification System for the required contractor class and specialist registration.

commonwealth.title: Register on AusTender and the Supplier Portal
commonwealth.applies_when: Finding Commonwealth opportunities, plans, panels and awards.
commonwealth.action: Create the account, alerts and supplier profile. Keep business characteristics accurate; the Supplier Portal opened to all businesses from July 2026.

commonwealth.title: Know whether the entity is an Australian business
commonwealth.applies_when: Commonwealth procurement rules give Australian businesses or SMEs a defined pathway.
commonwealth.action: Be ready to evidence ownership or Australian market listing, Australian tax residence and the principal place of business in Australia.

commonwealth.title: Prepare for the Commonwealth Supplier Code
commonwealth.applies_when: Commonwealth forms of contract, subject to documented exceptions.
commonwealth.action: Build proportionate evidence for ethics, conflicts, governance, tax, records, WHS, workplace rights, human rights, environment, security and subcontractor compliance.

commonwealth.title: Run the procurement-connected policy triggers
commonwealth.applies_when: The entity size, contract value, category, location or funding activates an extra policy.
commonwealth.action: Check the live request and the Finance policy table for Indigenous participation, tax records, payment times, gender equality, skills, environmental plans and Australian industry participation.

commonwealth.title: Treat security as scope-specific
commonwealth.applies_when: The work handles government information, systems, facilities, people, Defence assets or classified material.
commonwealth.action: Read the contract security schedule. Do not claim Essential Eight, IRAP, clearances, PSPF alignment or DISP membership unless the evidence exists and the requirement applies.

triggered_overlays.trigger: Commonwealth non-construction procurement by a non-corporate Commonwealth entity at $125,000 or more
triggered_overlays.effect: Division 2 of the Commonwealth Procurement Rules generally applies unless an exemption applies.

triggered_overlays.trigger: Non-construction procurement by a prescribed corporate Commonwealth entity at $400,000 or more
triggered_overlays.effect: Division 2 generally applies unless an exemption applies.

triggered_overlays.trigger: Commonwealth construction services procurement at $7.5 million or more
triggered_overlays.effect: Division 2 generally applies unless an exemption applies.

triggered_overlays.trigger: Commonwealth procurement valued at $4 million or more
triggered_overlays.effect: The approach may require satisfactory Statements of Tax Record for the tenderer and known first-tier subcontractors.

triggered_overlays.trigger: A tenderer with 100 or more Australian employees and a procurement at or above the relevant Commonwealth threshold
triggered_overlays.effect: A WGEA letter of compliance may be required with the submission or before contract.

triggered_overlays.trigger: Remote Commonwealth procurement, or other procurement wholly delivered in Australia valued from $80,000 to $200,000 GST inclusive
triggered_overlays.effect: The Indigenous Procurement Policy Mandatory Set Aside applies, subject to stated exceptions.

triggered_overlays.trigger: Commonwealth contract wholly delivered in Australia valued at $7.5 million or more in one of 19 specified industries
triggered_overlays.effect: Mandatory Minimum Indigenous Participation Requirements apply.

triggered_overlays.trigger: Eligible Commonwealth construction, maintenance or ICT procurement valued at $10 million or more
triggered_overlays.effect: Australian Skills Guarantee targets may apply.

triggered_overlays.trigger: Commonwealth construction procurement at $7.5 million or more, or covered furniture, ICT goods or textiles procurement at $1 million or more
triggered_overlays.effect: A Supplier Environmental Sustainability Plan and reporting may be required.

triggered_overlays.trigger: Commonwealth procurement valued at $20 million or more
triggered_overlays.effect: The successful tenderer may need a Commonwealth Australian Industry Participation plan.

triggered_overlays.trigger: Defence tender or contract requiring classified access, weapons or explosive ordnance, base security services, or DISP as a contract condition
triggered_overlays.effect: The required Defence Industry Security Program membership level must be in place.

strategic_examples.title: Windemere skate bowl refurbishment
strategic_examples.status: Active council tender; internal finish line 5 August 2026; official close 2:00 pm 6 August 2026
strategic_examples.role_model: VFG Skateparks leads technical delivery; Luke runs local bid systems and digital evidence; qualified specialists own regulated sign-off.
strategic_examples.next_action: Complete the requirements matrix, field-proof Aura Scan to Twin, lock specialist evidence and freeze the approved response before portal day.

strategic_examples.title: Dunwich (Gumpi) Ferry Terminal Upgrade
strategic_examples.status: $41 million SEQ City Deal commitment in planning; business case expected in late 2026
strategic_examples.role_model: Prepare qualified local packages and partner with civil, marine, building, design and environmental primes able to carry the main contract.
strategic_examples.next_action: Track the project and procurement pipeline, map likely work packages and build prequalification, company, evidence and partner readiness before release.

strategic_examples.title: Sandworm and Grain by Grain
strategic_examples.status: Long-horizon proposal and capability programme, not a current government project or tender
strategic_examples.role_model: Use research, simulation, robotics, maker training, digital twins and material testing to build future supplier capability rung by rung.
strategic_examples.next_action: Separate proposed outcomes from evidence, define testable work packages and build the material, engineering, approvals and partner chain.

human_gates: A human confirms the exact legal tenderer and authorised signatory.
A human reads every addendum and confirms mandatory attendance, format and deadline rules.
A qualified person confirms licences, engineering, safety, insurance, tax, employment, privacy and security claims.
Every partner approves its role, price, evidence, intellectual property and public/private boundary.
A human approves the final price, departures, declarations and contract-risk position.
Only an authorised human lodges the response and retains the portal receipt.
No LLM accepts a contract, signs a declaration, invents evidence or silently changes a lodged response.
